angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 130,026 km at 1.83 pc = 0.95 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 546.9759 +/- 0.0401 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 1.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.1869 +/- 0.0012 solar radii from Boyajian et al. Mass 0.146 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: mass 0.146 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3222 +/- 10 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: effective temperature in K, 3222 +/- 10, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
